clue.text: Star famed for converting country property

indicators.note: converting means changing form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous celebrity turns a rural house into a showpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for converting' rearranges STAR plus FAMED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhouse with its outbuildings is a rural holding, a piece of land and buildings in the countryside.

clue.text: One going from bank to bank, but keeping afloat

definitions.text: One going from bank to bank, but keeping afloat

parts.words: One going from bank to bank, but keeping afloat
parts.note: sounds like a debtor moving money between lenders while staying solvent, but the banks are river banks and afloat is literal

explanation.surface: A struggling borrower shifts accounts between lenders to stay solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' and 'afloat' both have financial senses that point to money troubles; read literally, it is a vessel crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is a vessel that shuttles passengers across water from one shore to the other.

clue.text: Come round repeatedly about a dog

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A stray mongrel keeps coming back to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again and again is to come round repeatedly, like a returning illness.

clue.text: Pen music for the last act

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a song is a piece of music

explanation.surface: A composer writes the score for the final scene of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a verb meaning write; it is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A final performance or work before retirement is called by this name, after the legend that swans sing before dying.

clue.text: Compromise to stop acrimony

parts.note: to stop is to end
acrimony is bitterness, anger

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a middle way to halt the bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compromise' is the verb meaning put at risk, not a settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety is to put it in danger, to imperil it.

clue.text: Unsympathetic about a listener being so cheerless

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: dry can mean cold and unsympathetic in manner
an ear is the organ one listens with

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted person ignores someone who would listen, which makes them gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsympathetic' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is 'cheerless' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and gloomy, lacking any brightness or joy.

clue.text: Collect for a service

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A church takes up a collection during worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like a noun, the short prayer said at a service, but it is the verb meaning gather.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together or accumulate, as wealth or evidence.

clue.text: Jack, a painter, reversing the mount

indicators.note: reversing means the whole string built from these pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so jack gives TAR
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A sailor and an artist turn back from climbing a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the mountain in Turkey where Noah's ark came to rest.

clue.text: An accessory only when in shabby attire

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
shabby means worn and out of shape, so the letters of attire are disordered

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: Someone wears a single accessory with their worn-out clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shabby' turns the letters of the clothing word into ATTRIE before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An object traditionally carried by a figure in art, like a saint's symbol, is an attribute.

clue.text: Skinhead getting on top of goody-goody youth

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: read as skin's head, the first letter of skin
a prig is a self-righteous goody-goody

explanation.surface: A skinhead bullies a sanctimonious teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' looks like the thug; read as the head of 'skin' it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is an old word for a young man, a stripling.

clue.text: He's clear about fish

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to rid is to clear
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: A man claims to be fine with seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' just asks for a man's name, so any male first name fitting the letters will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so any male could be referred to by it.

clue.text: Did he at one time tread the boards as Shylock?

definitions.text: Did he at one time tread the boards

explanation.surface: Was Shylock once played by a stage performer?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EX-ACTOR it is someone who used to act; as one word it is one who demands payment, like Shakespeare's moneylender.
explanation.definitionFit: A former stage performer, and also an extortioner who insists on what is owed, as Shylock does with his pound of flesh.

clue.text: Any Presbyterians in Belgium? Some

indicators.note: some means a part of the words is taken, the letters running inside them

explanation.surface: Asks whether there are any Presbyterians in Belgium, and answers that there are a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres is a town in West Flanders, famous from the First World War.

clue.text: Grant Iran wanted — it could be, telling.

indicators.note: it could be suggests the letters might form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recounts that a grant was wanted by Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' rearranges GRANT plus IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a story is recounting it, giving an account.

clue.text: No creditor accepts a plant

parts.note: O, nought, means no or nothing

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a lender is a creditor

explanation.surface: A creditor refuses to take a loan back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts A inside LENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous evergreen shrub with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: This is developing into a mean proceeding

indicators.note: developing means growing into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A situation is turning nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges INTO A MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that issues or flows out from a source is a proceeding from it.

clue.text: Barely deserved

explanation.surface: Only just got what was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Only just' means barely, and a fair reward is a deserved one.

clue.text: Hide their output

parts.note: seems to say keep production secret, but hide is animal skin, the product of places that cure leather

explanation.surface: Someone tells factories to conceal what they make.
explanation.definitionFit: Works where animal skins are cured into leather.

clue.text: Scrambling for liver, cat is standing upright

indicators.note: scrambling means mixing up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat stands on its hind legs, fighting for a piece of liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambling' rearranges LIVER plus CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpendicular to the ground, like a post that is upright.

clue.text: Matching one in green with silver borders

indicators.note: borders means forms the edges around, so silver goes round the rest

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in green with silver trim looks coordinated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside GREEN, then 'borders' puts A and G round that.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that correspond or match are in agreement with each other.

clue.text: A horse-drawn carriage not all can reverse

indicators.note: reverse means read the word backwards

parts.note: part means not all of something

explanation.surface: Not everyone can back a horse and cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can reverse' turns PART round.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a pony.

clue.text: Environment-friendly in the main?

parts.note: seems to describe ecology on the whole, but the main is the ocean and environment-friendly is a shade name, so a colour of the ocean

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is mostly eco-friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly'; the main is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluish-green colour like the ocean.

clue.text: A warning that includes military force

indicators.note: includes means takes in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British military force

explanation.surface: A caution that the army might be used.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army, a standard crossword source of two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A menacing declaration of harm to come serves as a warning.

clue.text: Imprisonment of holy man by a nobleman causes trouble

indicators.note: imprisonment means locking inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman
St, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A lord jailing a cleric stirs up unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother or harass someone persistently is to trouble them.

clue.text: Shame quiet fellows into a strike

indicators.note: into means put inside, so these pieces go within the other

parts.note: to bat is to strike a ball
sh is a call for quiet
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Workers are silenced and humiliated into walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shame' looks like a verb, but it is the noun the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment or disconcertion, a feeling of shame.

clue.text: Warning for a trainee preceding a member

indicators.note: preceding means coming before, so these letters come first

parts.note: L is a learner, as on an L-plate
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A caution given to a new recruit ahead of joining.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain, so L is a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal or sound that warns of danger.

clue.text: Read directions, before fitting supply

indicators.note: before means this piece comes first

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
due means fitting or proper

explanation.surface: Advice to read the instructions before assembling something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' only dresses the surface as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone with a quality is to furnish or provide them with it.

clue.text: The dog has to leave after a row!

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: The dog must be put out following a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow here: a racket, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild dog native to Australia.

clue.text: Finding pieces of metal in fodder

indicators.note: pieces of means broken into bits, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Discovering scraps of metal in animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of' rearranges METAL IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or nourishment, of which animal feed is a kind.

clue.text: Greek character not in favour of alcoholic drink

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: A Greek man refuses to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: An artistic individual, married, with a 19

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, a horse-drawn carriage, also means a snare, which a net is

explanation.surface: A creative person, wed, with a small carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 19 gives its answer's other sense, a snare, so NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard Manet was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: "Man is by his constitution a ——animal" (Burke)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Edmund Burke's Reflections on the Revolution in France, with the missing adjective as the answer

explanation.surface: A quotation from Burke about human nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a long dash for the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Burke held that faith in God is part of human nature, so the gap is the adjective for devout belief.
